q: Fuels made from oil mixtures contain large hydrocarbon molecules and are not ____ .
e: Efficiency in fuel refers to how well it burns and produces energy.

q: Consequently, cracking is important to convert the larger hydrocarbon molecules to ____ ones.
e: Smaller molecules are often more useful as fuels and in chemical processes.

q: When a catalyst is used, this process is called ____ cracking.
e: Catalytic cracking enhances the breakdown of hydrocarbons, improving fuel quality.

q: Cracking is a thermal decomposition process in which large alkane hydrocarbon molecules are broken down by passing them over a heated ____ under pressure.
e: Catalysts speed up chemical reactions without being consumed, making processes more efficient.

q: The products are smaller alkanes used for fuels (e.g., petrol or diesel) and ____ which are used to make polymers.
e: Alkenes are valuable for producing plastics and other synthetic materials.

q: The alkane produced from cracking may be straight chain alkanes which turn to branched isomer on heating with the ____ .
e: Catalysts can facilitate isomerization, enhancing fuel performance.

q: The higher the octane number, the greater the fuel's resistance to ____ in an internal combustion engine.
e: Knocking can reduce engine efficiency and cause damage, making octane ratings important.
